survival_report.system_diagnosis: Zero buys, zero passes: in the ~10 hours since the bot restarted onto the operator's 2026-07-02 security recalibration, 764 candidates were checked and every single one was blocked -- 0% pass rate. Traced this to a real bug, not bad luck: the code that is supposed to ignore a token's liquidity-pool/bonding-curve holdings when checking 'is one wallet holding too much of this token' has never actually worked. It looks up who owns the top-holder account, but the lookup always comes back with the same generic answer (the token program) instead of telling us whether that holder is a real whale or just the trading pool itself. So the pool's own holdings get counted as 'one wallet owns way too much,' and almost everything gets blocked. The operator's threshold changes yesterday were correct and are live, but they don't help because the underlying number they're checking against is inflated by this pre-existing bug.

research_findings.headline: WC convergence count is INVERTED: 3-wallet convergences win (N=30, 53%WR, +0.12% median) while 4+ wallets LOSE (N=12, 25%WR, -3.65% avg; 5+ = -7.56%) -- crowded convergences are late exit-liquidity traps, a separator no gate has ever used inside the bot's only profitable strategy.

new_hypothesis.name: lean_convergence_edge
new_hypothesis.mechanism: Inside wallet_convergence (the bot's sole edge), the NUMBER of tracked smart-wallets that converge on a token is INVERSELY related to outcome. Convergences of exactly 3 wallets win ~53% (+0.12% median); convergences of 4+ wallets win only ~25% and lose -3.65% avg; 5+ is -7.56% avg. By the time a 4th/5th/6th tracked wallet has piled into the same name, the move is already discovered -- you are buying the exit liquidity those very wallets will sell into. A lean 3-wallet convergence catches the signal while it is still early/contrarian.
new_hypothesis.persistence: Structural, not arbitrage-fragile: it is a property of WHEN in a token's life the convergence completes. Crowded convergence = late = the alpha wallets are now the exit. This persists as long as smart-money front-runs retail, which is the entire premise copy-trading rests on. It is the bot's own funnel-position, not a public signal, so it cannot be arbitraged away.
new_hypothesis.entry_rules: On a wallet_convergence trigger, count the distinct tracked wallets that bought within the convergence window. ENTER only if count is 2-3. SKIP if count >= 4. Optional stack: also require vol_liq_ratio < 15 (the 3-wallet AND vol_liq<15 cell was N=19, 63%WR, +4.1% avg in the subagent cut). Note vol_liq>=12 is already partly blocked by the live froth ceiling, so the marginal new gate is the count<=3 rule.
new_hypothesis.data_required: The converged-wallet COUNT. Currently recoverable ONLY by regex on the free-text 'reasoning' field of WC records; it is NOT a clean numeric field, and the 'WC N=10' token in reasoning is a static config param, not the live count. Implementation should add a numeric converged_wallet_count field (see proposal #2).
new_hypothesis.evidence: Mined all 42 completed WC round-trips in sol_trade_log.json (2116 entries) two independent ways. Brain reproduction: nwall==3 N=30 WR=53% avg=+0.07% median=+0.12%; nwall>=4 N=12 WR=25% avg=-3.65% median=-0.56%; nwall>=5 N=5 WR=20% avg=-7.56%. Subagent cut: nwall==3 N=26 54%WR +0.7%; nwall>=4 N=16 31% -3.7%; 3-AND-vol_liq<15 N=19 63%WR +4.1% vs rest N=23 30%WR -5.2%. Direction consistent across WR, mean AND median in both cuts. WC baseline overall: 42T 45.2%WR ~-1.0% avg.
